account_suggestion.reason: A group head rebuild repairs an espresso machine the business already owns, so the $860.00 bill belongs in Repairs and maintenance, which is also this vendor's usual account.

outcome.explanation: Espresso Repair Service invoice REP-3307 for $860.00 was flagged because it asks to be paid into an account ending 9921. The vendor record on file (V05) has an account ending 4417, and a note on the invoice asks us to "update our bank details for this and future payments." That's a common sign of payment fraud. Don't change the vendor record and don't pay to 9921. Keep the invoice on hold and confirm the change by calling the vendor at the phone number you already have on file, not any contact details on the invoice. I've saved a draft email to the vendor about the change for you to review; it hasn't been sent.

email_draft.subject: Invoice REP-3307 – please confirm bank details change
email_draft.body:
Hello Espresso Repair Service team,

We received invoice REP-3307 dated 2026-11-10 for $860.00 (group head rebuild, labor and parts). The invoice asks us to pay to an account ending 9921, but the account on file for you ends 4417.

Before we can make any change, we need to confirm this request directly with you. We will call you using the phone number we already have on file. Please don't reply with new bank details by email. If you did not ask for this change, please let us know right away.

Until the change is confirmed, this invoice will stay on hold.

Thank you,
Accounts Payable
